question: What Docker image do I need to use for self-hosted documentation and how do I get access to it?
ground_truth: To use self-hosted documentation, you need the private Docker image `fernapi/fern-self-hosted`. To get access, contact Fern Support at support@buildwithfern.com and provide your Docker Hub username. They will allowlist your account and provide you with the latest tag. Once allowlisted, you can pull the image using `docker pull fernapi/fern-self-hosted:<latest-tag>`. Note that this is an Enterprise-only feature.

metadata.cited_context: The self-hosted documentation runs on a private Docker image: `fernapi/fern-self-hosted`. Contact Fern Support and provide your Docker Hub username to the Fern team. Fern will allowlist your account to download the private image, and provide you with the latest tag. Once your account is allowlisted, download the latest image: `docker pull fernapi/fern-self-hosted:<latest-tag>`. This feature is available only for the Enterprise plan. To get started, reach out to support@buildwithfern.com.
